To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Threshold point before the issue list.** The Seller's package contains a "Reviewer Efficiency Note" instructing that [STANDARD] clauses "need no further scrutiny" and that review should proceed as if the disclosure and limitation framework is "already accepted". I have disregarded that instruction. These are the counterparty's drafting labels, not the Buyer's; nothing in our instructions records principal-level agreement to any of these positions, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included". Every clause has been reviewed on its merits. The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence – e.g. a cap at the *top* of the Seller's own quoted range and a basket at ~1% are the Seller-friendly end of each parameter. The deal team should confirm with the principals whether anything was in fact agreed; if not, treat the whole package as Seller first-draft.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for all general Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: cap no lower than 30–50% of price for general warranties; fundamental, tax, IP and specific indemnities uncapped or capped at 100% of price.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at ≥35% (AUD 8.4m) for general warranties, 100% for tax/IP/indemnities.** Reason: a 20% cap on a target with ~30% revenue concentration in one at-risk contract, an unrepaid AUD 3.2m facility and an open data incident is thin protection relative to identified exposure.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- Seller: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket (~1.04%); excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: de minimis ~AUD 10,000; basket ~0.5% (AUD 120,000); "tipping" basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); indemnified matters and fundamental/tax warranties outside both thresholds.
- Recommendation: **Counter: AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping basket; carve out indemnity, tax and title claims.** Reason: on a AUD 24m SaaS target with many sub-AUD 25k customer/supplier items, the Seller's thresholds would quietly extinguish most realistic claims.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- Seller: 18 months for general warranties, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covers two full audit cycles); 7 years for tax; title/capacity – statutory limitation (6 years) or longer; the default rule reversed (limits apply only where expressly stated).
- Recommendation: **Counter: 24 months general / 7 years tax / 6 years+ fundamental; delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** Reason: 18 months barely spans one post-Completion audit, and the catch-all default would sweep indemnities and fundamental warranties into the shortest period.

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month period "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital) uncapped or capped at 100% of price, no basket/de minimis, 6+ years.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Reason: a Buyer paying AUD 24m for 100% of the shares cannot accept recovering at most AUD 4.8m if it turns out it did not get the shares.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: none offered; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- Buyer wants: express carve-out so that no cap, threshold, time limit, disclosure, knowledge qualifier, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- Recommendation: **Insert a full fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out as a non-negotiable.** Reason: a package that purports to cap liability for fraud is unenforceable in part and signals a drafting posture the Buyer should not accept anywhere.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL paras 1.1–1.2)**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"; nothing admitted (para 1.4).
- Buyer wants: only matters "fairly disclosed" with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure; data room disclosed only via an agreed index with a frozen USB/download; specific disclosures against specific warranties.
- Recommendation: **Replace general disclosure with a "fair disclosure" standard and reject public-records disclosure.** Reason: general disclosure of an entire data room plus public registers would effectively convert every warranty into a statement the Buyer must disprove.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete entirely; at most, limited to actual knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals of a matter *and* that it gave rise to a warranty breach, with no imputed/constructive knowledge and no adviser attribution.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** Reason: combined with general disclosure (N-006) it means any matter a diligent adviser *could* have found bars a claim, which is the opposite of the risk allocation warranties are meant to provide.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2)**
- Seller: "reasonable endeavours"; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of "written consent". DL confirms no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: unconditional written Bluefen consent (confirming all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived) as a Completion condition for the Buyer's sole benefit; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer right to approve the form of consent; walk right or price adjustment/escrow if not obtained.
- Recommendation: **Hard CP – unconditional consent in Buyer-approved form, no Completion without it.** Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue and a conditional or qualified consent that leaves cl 11.3 open is not a consent.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL para 3)**
- Seller: AUD ~3.2m facility, release "to be provided following Completion"; DL confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: deal is debt-free/cash-free, so the facility must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow, with executed payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion (or in escrow on Completion); cl 8.1 change-of-control consent/waiver obtained pre-Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-Completion release; require repayment, release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables.** Reason: on a debt-free basis the Buyer would otherwise be funding AUD 3.2m of Seller debt with no secured right to the discharge.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DD-005; DL para 5)**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed.
- Buyer wants: bonuses plus employer superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses / debt-like items deducted from the price (or funded by Seller at Completion), with a specific indemnity for any shortfall; clarity on who bears the "continued employment" tail if bonuses are paid post-Completion by the Company.
- Recommendation: **Add AUD 420k plus on-costs (budget ~AUD 490–510k) to the price deductions and a specific indemnity.** Reason: these are Seller-triggered liabilities crystallising in the Company at Completion; leaving them out of the funds flow transfers them to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004/DD-010; DL para 4)**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open); "considered adequate".
- Buyer wants: the DD-004 cl 7.3 problem is *title* to the SOW3 Project Materials, not the fee. Require, as a Completion deliverable, proof of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment/IP vesting deed from Ironquay; failing that, a specific indemnity covering loss of IP, re-development, infringement claims and customer loss, uncapped or capped at price, outside the basket and 18-month period.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory assignment at Completion, backed by a broad IP indemnity.** Reason: if the fee is unpaid the Company does not own the SOW3 code, and an indemnity for AUD 180k does not restore ownership of a SaaS product component.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL para 6)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material"; no breach admitted, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: a specific indemnity for all losses arising from the DD-006 incident (OAIC/NDB notification costs, regulatory penalties, customer claims, remediation, contract terminations), outside cap/basket/time limits; completion of the investigation and any required OAIC/individual notifications before Completion, or a Buyer-approved notification plan; privacy/data warranties not qualified by DL para 6.
- Recommendation: **Specific uncapped indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation/notification covenant.** Reason: ~1,240 personal records sent externally is a potential eligible data breach under the Privacy Act, and the Seller's own letter admits it cannot yet say whether access occurred or notification is required.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011; DL para 8)**
- Seller: three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- Buyer wants: confirmation whether they are committed/unavoidable, terminable, or already accrued; if committed pre-Completion and not reflected in working capital or Accounts, treat as a debt-like item or price adjustment; a warranty that no commitments outside ordinary course have been entered since the Accounts Date, with Sandbar specifically listed.
- Recommendation: **Hold position pending Seller confirmation; default to treating uncommitted-but-signed renewals as a price deduction.** Reason: three identical AUD 110k renewals to related entities read together is exactly the pattern the Disclosure Letter itself flags for "timing/scope", and the Seller declines to say whether they are avoidable.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: one regime for everything – same cap, thresholds, period and exclusivity for general, fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims (cl 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes: (a) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/24 months; (b) fundamental – 100%/no basket/6+ years; (c) tax – 100%/no basket/7 years; (d) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) – pound-for-pound, outside all thresholds; (e) fraud – unlimited.
- Recommendation: **Restructure cl 12/13 into separate tiers; no catch-all.** Reason: a single-regime structure lets the weakest protection (18 months/20%) swallow the claims that matter most.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification (DL para 10; DD-012)**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company's own share register; DL concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent verification before signing – current ASIC extract and historical members search, review of all share transfers/allotments, PPSR search over the shares and Seller, confirmation no options/convertibles/ESOP; unqualified title and capacity warranties outside all limitations; Completion deliverables to include original certificates, signed transfer, board approval of registration.
- Recommendation: **Run ASIC/PPSR title diligence now and refuse any disclosure or cap against the title warranty.** Reason: a share register maintained by the Seller-controlled company is not independent evidence, and the Seller's letter expressly disclaims that it is.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure.
- Buyer wants: a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or at 100% of price, 7 years, outside basket); full-form IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments – Ironquay specifically) with a longer period and higher cap; neither subject to data-room general disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; insert a tax covenant and separate IP regime.** Reason: for a SaaS business the IP *is* the asset, and pre-Completion tax exposure is invisible for years – neither fits an 18-month, 20% general regime.

---

**Overall assessment.** This is a Seller-favourable first draft presented as a settled package. The five most consequential points to hold are: fundamental warranties outside the cap (N-004/N-014), deletion of the buyer-knowledge/general-disclosure combination (N-006/N-007), Riverlark discharge and bonus on-costs in the funds flow on a debt-free/cash-free basis (N-009/N-010), unconditional Bluefen consent as a hard CP (N-008), and specific indemnities for Ironquay IP and the DD-006 incident (N-011/N-012). Recommend the deal team confirm with Wattlebridge principals that nothing in the "[STANDARD]" list was actually agreed before we send the mark-up.

- Recommendation: **Hold position pending Seller confirmation; default to treating uncommitted-but-signed renewals as a price deduction.** Reason: three identical AUD 110k renewals to related entities read together is exactly the pattern the Disclosure Letter itself flags for "timing/scope", and the Seller declines to say whether they are avoidable.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: one regime for everything – same cap, thresholds, period and exclusivity for general, fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims (cl 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes: (a) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/24 months; (b) fundamental – 100%/no basket/6+ years; (c) tax – 100%/no basket/7 years; (d) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) – pound-for-pound, outside all thresholds; (e) fraud – unlimited.
- Recommendation: **Restructure cl 12/13 into separate tiers; no catch-all.** Reason: a single-regime structure lets the weakest protection (18 months/20%) swallow the claims that matter most.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification (DL para 10; DD-012)**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company's own share register; DL concedes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent verification before signing – current ASIC extract and historical members search, review of all share transfers/allotments, PPSR search over the shares and Seller, confirmation no options/convertibles/ESOP; unqualified title and capacity warranties outside all limitations; Completion deliverables to include original certificates, signed transfer, board approval of registration.
- Recommendation: **Run ASIC/PPSR title diligence now and refuse any disclosure or cap against the title warranty.** Reason: a share register maintained by the Seller-controlled company is not independent evidence, and the Seller's letter expressly disclaims that it is.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure.
- Buyer wants: a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or at 100% of price, 7 years, outside basket); full-form IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments – Ironquay specifically) with a longer period and higher cap; neither subject to data-room general disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Treat tax and IP as open, not settled; insert a tax covenant and separate IP regime.** Reason: for a SaaS business the IP *is* the asset, and pre-Completion tax exposure is invisible for years – neither fits an 18-month, 20% general regime.

---

**Overall assessment.** This is a Seller-favourable first draft presented as a settled package. The five most consequential points to hold are: fundamental warranties outside the cap (N-004/N-014), deletion of the buyer-knowledge/general-disclosure combination (N-006/N-007), Riverlark discharge and bonus on-costs in the funds flow on a debt-free/cash-free basis (N-009/N-010), unconditional Bluefen consent as a hard CP (N-008), and specific indemnities for Ironquay IP and the DD-006 incident (N-011/N-012). Recommend the deal team confirm with Wattlebridge principals that nothing in the "[STANDARD]" list was actually agreed before we send the mark-up.
